reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space E, every potential U : E -> R, every alpha and eta in NNReal, and every reference point xref in E, assume 0 < alpha <= 1, eta <= 1, U is C^2, alpha * ||v||^2 <= D^2 U(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2 for every x,v in E, and ||gradient U(xref)||^2 <= alpha * finrank_R(E). Let mu be the normalized exponential tilt of volume by -U (when its normalizing integral is finite), and let piEta be the Gaussian smoothing of mu with standard deviation sqrt(eta). Then phaseWassersteinSq at parameter 1/alpha between (dirac xref) product (standard Gaussian on E) and piEta product (standard Gaussian on E) is at most ENNReal.ofReal(5 * (1/alpha) * finrank_R(E)).
objects: A finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space E; potential U : E -> R; nonnegative reals alpha and eta; reference point xref in E; tilted volume law mu; smoothed law piEta; standard Gaussian momentum law on E.
domains: E has the stated finite-dimensional, complete, inner-product, and Borel structure; U : E -> R; alpha, eta : NNReal; xref : E; x and v range over E in the Hessian condition.
quantifiers: Universal over E, U, alpha, eta, and xref; universal over x,v in the Hessian condition. There is no supplied or existentially asserted minimizer or critical point in this statement.
assumptions: 0 < alpha <= 1; eta <= 1, allowing eta = 0; U is C^2 (ContDiff R 2 U); for all x,v in E, alpha * ||v||^2 <= D^2 U(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2; ||gradient U(xref)||^2 <= alpha * finrank_R(E).
conclusion: The squared phase quadratic Kantorovich infimum phaseWassersteinSq (1/alpha) between (Measure.dirac xref).prod (stdGaussian E) and piEta.prod (stdGaussian E) is <= ENNReal.ofReal(5 * (1/alpha) * finrank_R(E)), where mu = volume.tilted(-U) and piEta = gaussianSmoothing mu (sqrt eta).
scopes: Only a q=2 squared-cost transport bound for these phase-space product laws. The same standard Gaussian momentum appears in both laws. No minimizer or critical point is an input; no all-q concentration, Picard transition, final total-variation accuracy, or expected-query-cost claim is stated. The tilt is normalized when its normalizing integral is finite; finiteness is not a separate displayed hypothesis.
constant_dependencies: The explicit upper bound is 5 * finrank_R(E) / alpha, embedded by ENNReal.ofReal. Its numeric factor is 5; it has no displayed dependence on eta, xref, or U beyond the hypotheses. The cost parameter is 1/alpha and smoothing standard deviation is sqrt(eta).
